info.title: API.SH: PCPartPicker
info.description: The PCPartPicker API from API.SH: public PCPartPicker data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
One completed build on PCPartPicker: name, author, every part with its component type, link, image and price, the total, the build's details (date published, clock rates, temperatures…), description, photos, comments and the link to its full part list. `latest=true` opens the top-rated build of the past month.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/pcpartpicker-build

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Regional site: us (pcpartpicker.com, default) or a country code such as uk, ca, au, de, fr; prices come from that country's shops in its currency. A regional link picks its site.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Build id (`id` in builds) or its pcpartpicker.com/b/... link.

parameters.name: latest
parameters.description: `true`: the top-rated build of the past month.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Completed PC builds on PCPartPicker with every filter and sort of the builds page: keywords, published period (`filter_period`: `1d`, `1w`, `1m`, `1y`), featured builds, CPU cooler type, overclocked CPU, CPU socket, video card chipset, case type and price range. `filters` lists each filter's `param`, ids and range. Each build: `id`, `url`, `name`, `image`, `author`, `key_parts`, `price`, `votes`, `comments`. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/pcpartpicker-builds

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Regional site: us (pcpartpicker.com, default) or a country code such as uk, ca, au, de, fr; prices come from that country's shops in its currency. A regional link picks its site.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order.

parameters.name: filter_period

parameters.name: price_min
parameters.description: Build price at least (in the regional site's currency; US dollars by default).

parameters.name: price_max
parameters.description: Build price at most (in the regional site's currency; US dollars by default).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number. Pass `next_page` from the previous response; null on the last page.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
PC parts in one PCPartPicker category (pcpartpicker.com or a regional site, prices in its currency) with every filter and sort of the category page: keywords, price range, and the category's own filters (manufacturer, socket, core count, chipset, memory, rating…). `filters` lists each filter with its `param` name (e.g. `filter_m` for manufacturer), its item ids or its range; pass ids comma separated (`filter_m=6,21`) or a range as `min,max`. `sorts` lists the valid sorts (`price`, `-price`, `rating`, spec columns). Each part: `id`, `name`, `url`, `image`, `price` (lowest US price), `rating`, `rating_count` and the category's key `specs`. Up to 100 parts a page; `total` is the site's count. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/pcpartpicker-products

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Regional site: us (pcpartpicker.com, default) or a country code such as uk, ca, au, de, fr; prices come from that country's shops in its currency. A regional link picks its site.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Part category.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Keywords, e.g. `ryzen`, `rtx 4070`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: A value from `sorts`, e.g. `price`, `-price`, `rating`, `-cores`.

parameters.name: price_min
parameters.description: Lowest price at least (in the regional site's currency; US dollars by default).

parameters.name: price_max
parameters.description: Lowest price at most (in the regional site's currency; US dollars by default).

parameters.name: filter_m
parameters.description: Manufacturer ids from `filters` (the `filter_m` entry), comma separated. Every other filter of the category works the same way with its own `param` from `filters`.

parameters.name: compatible_only
parameters.description: `false`: also list parts the site marks incompatible.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number. Pass `next_page` from the previous response; null on the last page.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
